people.cyrus.role: Persian king who lets the people rebuild the temple
people.cyrus.relations: He is king of Persia. He gives the temple vessels to Mithredath, who counts them out to Sheshbazzar.
people.cyrus.meaning: In his first year Cyrus sends an order through his kingdom. It says the LORD’s people may go to Jerusalem and build his house. He also brings out the vessels Nebuchadnezzar took. Later the builders and Darius both point back to this order.
people.jeremiah.role: Earlier prophet named in the book’s first verse
people.jeremiah.relations: The first verse names him beside Cyrus. He does not act in this book.
people.jeremiah.meaning: The LORD spoke a word by Jeremiah before this book begins. Verse 1 says the LORD stirred Cyrus so that word would come true.
people.nebuchadnezzar.role: King of Babylon who took the people and the vessels
people.nebuchadnezzar.relations: He is king of Babylon. Cyrus later brings out the vessels he took.
people.nebuchadnezzar.meaning: He took the temple vessels from Jerusalem. He put them in the house of his gods. He carried the people away to Babylon. The elders say he also destroyed the temple. The book begins when the people and the vessels come back.
people.sheshbazzar.role: Prince of Judah who carries the vessels home
people.sheshbazzar.relations: Chapter 1 calls him the prince of Judah. In chapter 5 the elders say Cyrus made him governor.
people.sheshbazzar.meaning: Mithredath counts the temple vessels out to him. He brings them up from Babylon to Jerusalem. The elders later say he laid the foundations of God’s house.
people.mithredath-treasurer.role: Treasurer who counts out the temple vessels
people.mithredath-treasurer.relations: He serves Cyrus as treasurer. He counts the vessels out to Sheshbazzar.
people.mithredath-treasurer.meaning: Cyrus brings out the temple vessels by his hand. Mithredath counts them out to Sheshbazzar. The list comes to 5,400 vessels of gold and silver.
people.zerubbabel.role: Leader who starts the altar and the temple
people.zerubbabel.relations: He is the son of Shealtiel. He works with Jeshua the son of Jozadak.
people.zerubbabel.meaning: His name stands first in the list of those who return. He and Jeshua build the altar and start the temple. He tells the neighbors they may not build with him. After Haggai and Zechariah speak, he starts building again.
people.jeshua-priest.role: Priest who builds the altar with Zerubbabel
people.jeshua-priest.relations: He is the son of Jozadak and works with Zerubbabel. Four of his family are named in chapter 10.
people.jeshua-priest.meaning: He and his brother priests build the altar with Zerubbabel. They offer burnt offerings and start the temple. He joins Zerubbabel in refusing the neighbors’ help. In chapter 10, four men of his family promise to send their foreign wives away.
people.returning-families.role: Families and temple workers counted in the return list
people.returning-families.relations: They come with Zerubbabel and Jeshua. The list names families, priests, Levites, singers, gatekeepers, and temple servants.
people.returning-families.meaning: They leave Babylon and go back to Jerusalem and Judah, each to his city. The whole group numbers 42,360. Some cannot show their fathers’ houses. Some priests are not found in the records and are kept from serving.
people.moses.role: Earlier leader whose law the people follow
people.moses.meaning: Moses does not act in this book. The builders set up the altar as his law says. Ezra is a skilled scribe in that same law.
people.david.role: Earlier king whose directions the singers follow
people.david.relations: The book calls him king of Israel. Hattush, of the sons of David, travels with Ezra.
people.david.meaning: David does not act in this book. The priests and Levites praise the LORD by his directions in chapter 3. Chapter 8 says he gave the temple servants to help the Levites.
people.asaph-singer.role: Earlier singer whose sons play at the foundation
people.asaph-singer.relations: The Levites with cymbals in 3:10 are called the sons of Asaph.
people.asaph-singer.meaning: Asaph does not act in this book. His sons play cymbals when the builders lay the temple’s foundation. They sing that the LORD is good.
people.darius-ezra.role: Persian king who lets the temple be finished
people.darius-ezra.relations: He is king of Persia. Tattenai and Shetharbozenai write to him, and he answers them.
people.darius-ezra.meaning: Work on the temple stops until his second year. Tattenai asks him to search for Cyrus’s order, and a scroll is found. Darius tells Tattenai to leave the work alone and pay its costs. The temple is finished in his sixth year.
people.ahasuerus-ezra.role: Persian king who is sent an accusation
people.ahasuerus-ezra.relations: He is named in one verse, between Darius and Artaxerxes.
people.ahasuerus-ezra.meaning: Ezra 4:6 is his only verse in this book. At the start of his reign, enemies write an accusation against Judah and Jerusalem. The book does not give his answer.
people.artaxerxes-ezra.role: Persian king who stops the city, then sends Ezra
people.artaxerxes-ezra.relations: He is king of Persia. Rehum and Shimshai write to him, and he later sends Ezra.
people.artaxerxes-ezra.meaning: Rehum and Shimshai warn him that Jerusalem is a rebel city. He orders the building to stop. In his seventh year he gives Ezra a letter. It lets Ezra carry silver and gold, teach the law, and appoint judges.
people.mithredath-writer.role: Man who writes to Artaxerxes with Bishlam and Tabeel
people.mithredath-writer.relations: He is named with Bishlam and Tabeel. He is not Mithredath the treasurer in chapter 1.
people.mithredath-writer.meaning: He writes to Artaxerxes with Bishlam, Tabeel, and their companions. The letter is in the Syrian language. The book does not give its words.
people.rehum-chancellor.relations: He writes with Shimshai the scribe and their companions. Artaxerxes answers them.
people.rehum-chancellor.meaning: He writes to Artaxerxes that Jerusalem is a rebel city. He says a finished city will pay no tribute. The king tells him to stop the builders. Rehum hurries to Jerusalem and stops them by force.
people.shimshai.role: Scribe who writes against Jerusalem with Rehum
people.shimshai.relations: He is a scribe. He writes with Rehum the chancellor to Artaxerxes.
people.shimshai.meaning: He and Rehum write a letter against Jerusalem to Artaxerxes. The king’s answer is read before them. They hurry to Jerusalem and stop the Jews by force.
people.haggai.role: Prophet who helps the builders start again
people.haggai.relations: He speaks at the same time as Zechariah. Zerubbabel and Jeshua build while he speaks.
people.haggai.meaning: Haggai speaks to the Jews in the name of the God of Israel. Zerubbabel and Jeshua then begin to build again. Chapter 6 says the elders built and did well through his words.
people.zechariah-prophet.role: Prophet who helps the builders start again
people.zechariah-prophet.relations: Ezra calls him the son of Iddo. He speaks at the same time as Haggai.
people.zechariah-prophet.meaning: Zechariah speaks to the Jews in the name of the God of Israel. Zerubbabel and Jeshua then begin to build again. Chapter 6 says the elders built and did well through his words.
people.tattenai.relations: He is the governor beyond the River. He works with Shetharbozenai and writes to Darius.
people.tattenai.meaning: He comes to the builders and asks who gave them an order to build. He asks for their names. He does not stop them, and he sends their answer to Darius. When Darius replies, Tattenai does what the king says.
people.shethar-bozenai.role: Official who questions the builders with Tattenai
people.shethar-bozenai.relations: The reading text spells his name Shetharbozenai. He is always named with Tattenai.
people.shethar-bozenai.meaning: He comes with Tattenai to ask who let the Jews build. He sends the letter to Darius with him. Darius tells them both to stay away from the work. They do what the king says.
people.ezra.role: Priest and scribe who teaches God’s law
people.ezra.relations: He is the son of Seraiah, and his line goes back to Aaron. Artaxerxes gives him a letter and gifts.
people.ezra.meaning: Ezra leaves Babylon with a letter from Artaxerxes. He fasts at the river Ahava. He brings the people and the gifts safely to Jerusalem. There he learns that many men have married foreign women. He tears his clothes and prays. Then he tells the men to separate from those wives.
people.aaron.role: Earlier chief priest at the head of Ezra’s line
people.aaron.meaning: Aaron does not act in this book. Ezra’s family list ends with him and calls him the chief priest.
people.iddo-casiphia.role: Chief at Casiphia whom Ezra asks for helpers
people.iddo-casiphia.relations: He is the chief at the place Casiphia. His brothers are the temple servants there.
people.iddo-casiphia.meaning: Ezra finds no sons of Levi in his camp. He sends eleven men to Iddo to ask for ministers for God’s house. Sherebiah, Hashabiah, their relatives, and 220 temple servants then join Ezra.
people.sherebiah.role: Levite who joins Ezra and guards the gifts
people.sherebiah.relations: He is of the sons of Mahli. He comes with his sons and brothers, eighteen in all.
people.sherebiah.meaning: He comes from Casiphia after Ezra asks for ministers. The text calls him a man of discretion. Ezra weighs the silver, gold, and vessels into his hands. He must guard them until they are weighed in Jerusalem.
people.hashabiah.role: Man from Casiphia who guards the gifts
people.hashabiah.relations: He comes with Jeshaiah of the sons of Merari. Twenty of their brothers and sons come too.
people.hashabiah.meaning: He comes from Casiphia after Ezra asks for ministers. Ezra sets him apart with Sherebiah and ten others. Ezra weighs the silver, gold, and vessels into their hands for the journey.
people.meremoth.role: Priest who takes the weighed gifts in Jerusalem
people.meremoth.relations: He is the son of Uriah the priest. Eleazar, Jozabad, and Noadiah are with him.
people.meremoth.meaning: On the fourth day in Jerusalem the gifts are weighed into his hand. This happens in the house of God. Everything is counted, and the weight is written down.
people.eleazar-phinehas.role: Man with Meremoth when the gifts are weighed
people.eleazar-phinehas.relations: He is the son of Phinehas. He stands with Meremoth, Jozabad, and Noadiah.
people.eleazar-phinehas.meaning: Ezra 8:33 is his only verse. He is with Meremoth when the silver, gold, and vessels are weighed in God’s house.
people.jozabad-ezra.role: Levite present when the gifts are weighed
people.jozabad-ezra.relations: He is the son of Jeshua and a Levite. He stands with Noadiah, Meremoth, and Eleazar.
people.jozabad-ezra.meaning: Ezra 8:33 is his only sure verse. He is with Meremoth when the silver, gold, and vessels are weighed in God’s house. Chapter 10 lists other men named Jozabad.
people.noadiah-ezra.role: Levite present when the gifts are weighed
people.noadiah-ezra.relations: He is the son of Binnui and a Levite. He stands with Jozabad, Meremoth, and Eleazar.
people.noadiah-ezra.meaning: Ezra 8:33 is his only verse. He is with Meremoth when the silver, gold, and vessels are weighed in God’s house.
people.foreign-wives-children.role: Women and children the men agree to send away
people.foreign-wives-children.relations: They are the wives and children of men listed in chapter 10. None of them is named.
people.foreign-wives-children.meaning: The princes tell Ezra that men of Israel have married women from nearby peoples. Shecaniah proposes sending away the wives and their children. The men swear to do it. The book gives none of the women’s or children’s words.
people.shecaniah-jehiel.role: Man who proposes sending the foreign wives away
people.shecaniah-jehiel.relations: He is the son of Jehiel, of the sons of Elam. He speaks to Ezra.
people.shecaniah-jehiel.meaning: He tells Ezra, “We have trespassed against our God.” He says there is still hope for Israel. He proposes a covenant to put away the wives and their children. Ezra then makes the leaders swear to do it.
people.jehohanan-eliashib.relations: He is the son of Eliashib. Ezra uses his room.
people.jehohanan-eliashib.meaning: Ezra 10:6 is his only verse. Ezra goes into his room after the leaders swear. There Ezra eats no bread and drinks no water. Jehohanan himself does nothing in the story.
people.marriage-objectors.role: Two men who stand against the plan in this translation
people.marriage-objectors.relations: Jonathan is the son of Asahel. Jahzeiah is the son of Tikvah. Meshullam and Shabbethai help them.
people.marriage-objectors.meaning: The people ask for set times to hear each case. Our reading text says only these two men stood against this. The Church Bible’s main text says they worked on the matter. The book does not give their reasons.
people.shabbethai.role: Levite who helps Jonathan and Jahzeiah
people.shabbethai.relations: He is a Levite. Ezra 10:15 names him with Meshullam, Jonathan, and Jahzeiah.
people.shabbethai.meaning: Ezra 10:15 is his only verse. He and Meshullam help Jonathan and Jahzeiah. In our reading text those two stand against the plan.
places.jerusalem.summary: Zerubbabel and Jeshua build the altar and the temple here in chapters 3 to 6. Ezra brings the gifts here in chapter 8. The people gather here in the rain in chapter 10.
places.jerusalem.limits: The marker shows the city’s general location.
places.babylon.summary: Nebuchadnezzar carried the people and the temple vessels here. Sheshbazzar brings the vessels back from here in chapter 1. Ezra leaves from here in chapter 7.
places.babylon.limits: The marker shows the city’s general location. The book also uses the name for the land around it.
places.sidon.summary: In chapter 3 the builders give food, drink, and oil to the people of Sidon. In return they bring cedar trees from Lebanon to the sea.
places.sidon.limits: The marker shows the city’s general location.
places.tyre.summary: In chapter 3 the builders give food, drink, and oil to the people of Tyre. In return they bring cedar trees from Lebanon to Joppa.
places.tyre.limits: The marker shows the city’s general location.
places.lebanon.summary: In chapter 3 the cedar trees for the temple come from Lebanon. The people of Sidon and Tyre bring them to the sea.
places.lebanon.limits: Lebanon is a wide mountain region. The marker shows only its general area.
places.joppa.summary: In chapter 3 the cedar trees from Lebanon come by sea to Joppa.
places.joppa.limits: The marker shows the town’s general location.
places.samaria.summary: In chapter 4 Rehum and Shimshai write for peoples settled in the city of Samaria. Artaxerxes sends his answer to their companions who live there.
places.samaria.limits: The marker shows the city’s general location.
sources.web.summary: A complete public-domain reading text for all ten chapters.
sources.web.limits: The text tells the story. It does not prove each event, name, or private belief.
sources.atlas.limits: Use the place labels as background. The linked atlas also includes LDS commentary.
sources.atlas-canaan.limits: The map points are estimates. A town marker does not prove that an event happened there.
sources.terrain.limits: Modern terrain helps show the land. It does not show ancient shorelines or settlements.
sources.luther-ezra.summary: The overview studies temple rebuilding, the community’s identity, and how the book is built.
sources.luther-ezra.limits: This source gives scholarly teaching background. Scholars still debate the editing dates, the author, and the meaning.
sources.havea-ezra.summary: Havea looks at the people who came back and the people who had stayed. He also looks at how community lines shut people out.
sources.havea-ezra.limits: This is one named reading with a modern comparison. It does not recover what each ancient person believed.
sources.eskenazi-excerpt.summary: Eskenazi studies how the community lasted, its scripture, and rebuilding under Persian rule. She also studies how the book is built.
sources.eskenazi-excerpt.limits: This publisher excerpt gives literary background. It does not show that scholars agree or prove every event.
sources.eskenazi-record.summary: Yale’s record confirms Eskenazi’s commentary, its publication date, and its ISBN.
sources.eskenazi-record.limits: The publisher description and publication details were reviewed. The full 504-page commentary was not read.
sources.mcclellan-ezra.summary: McClellan reads the foreign-marriage rule as guarding a community line after the exile.
sources.mcclellan-ezra.limits: The timestamp finds the section, not the exact words. This reading does not prove the wives’ beliefs. It is not Church teaching.
sources.wiki-ezra.summary: The opening gives the book’s structure and leads to a list of sources.
sources.wiki-ezra.limits: The opening four paragraphs were reviewed. Compare its broad history claims with scholarly sources.
sources.cfm-ezra-2026.limits: Faith teaching and application. Its Nehemiah 8 material does not cover Ezra 8.
sources.lds-ezra-intro.summary: The introduction gives Church teaching background on restoration. It also describes the two main parts of Ezra’s story.
sources.lds-ezra-intro.limits: This is a general book introduction, not verse-by-verse commentary. Its dates are approximate. Its possible Sheshbazzar identification remains uncertain.
sources.lds-ezra-104.summary: The lesson connects study, practice, teaching, prayer, and repentance. It reads the marriages through concern about idol worship.
sources.lds-ezra-104.limits: This LDS reading does not prove what each wife believed. The lesson says Ezra started from Shushan. The map starts him from Babylon, as Ezra 7 says.
sources.ezra-kjv-10.limits: The editions describe the men’s role differently. This comparison does not settle the Hebrew wording.
sources.met-327369.limits: It shows that this region used marked weights. It does not show the standard weight used in Israel.
chapters.*.mapNote: The points show chosen known places and broad regions. Ahava, Casiphia, and Achmetha have no points because their locations are not known here.
chapters.*.routeEvidence: The map draws no journey line. The book does not give the exact road.
